domain: development approval / first-instance development application (DA) decisions, South Australia statewide register
prediction_question: FIXED 2026-11-07 (label sources measured, see notes s6.2): at the lodgement instant of a development application lodged through the SA PlanSA portal, predict whether the application will be decided within the statutory timeframe applicable to its assessment pathway under the PDI Act 2016 (primary; a per-application version of the statutory-timeframe KPI that SA/Vic/NSW publish only as aggregate percentages), with the per-consent decision outcome (refusal) as a secondary label. Prospective user: an applicant or their planning professional at/before lodgement, and councils forecasting assessment workload; a useful prediction supports pre-lodgement advice and resource allocation. Both labels derive from the register's per-application DecisionDetails (decision type / decision / decision date), measured available 2026-11-07 on a verified example (app 6154: 'Development Approval / Granted / 30 Apr 2021', lodged 1 Apr 2021) via a machine-readable detail endpoint - but that channel was also measured to degrade to hollow responses under sustained querying (notes s6.3), so label-row availability rate under a paced extraction is the last unmeasured input.
prediction_time: At lodgement of the application. Features displayed by the register that are documented at that instant: description (free text, e.g. 'Commercial', 'Verandah', 'Outbuilding (domestic storage shed)'), Assessment Pathway (e.g. 'Accepted'), Elements (e.g. 'Internal fitout', Demolition/Land division/Telecom codes DM/LD/TF/TA/RDT), Council area, Decision authority type (Assessment Manager / Assessment Panel / Council / DAC / Governor / Independent Assessor / Minister / SCAP / State Planning Commission), Act (DEV/PDI), applicant name, property address and title. Post-lodgement fields to exclude from features: status, decision, decision date, notification outcome, and any post-hoc reclassification. Two timing questions remain unresolved: (1) whether the displayed Assessment Pathway/category is exactly the value assigned at lodgement or a later-revised value (needs the PDI Act guidance pages); (2) no decision DATE has yet been observed on a detail page (only the decision TYPE on the Assessment tab), which blocks candidate A's latency label. The register is a current-state service: it showed applications lodged 05/11/2026 by the 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z fetch, and historical vintages are not archived, so a task built from it is retrospective with an explicit as-of assumption; decisions may also change after the fact (status vocabulary contains 'Decision Under Appeal', 'Lapsed').
target_definition: FIXED family 2026-11-07; prevalence unmeasured. Primary label, binary: statutory-timeframe latency = decision date (DecisionDetails DD, e.g. '30 Apr 2021') minus lodged date exceeds the PDI Act assessment timeframe for the application's pathway. Pathway timeframes documented from the publisher's own 'Stages and timeframes' page (read 2026-11-07): deemed-to-satisfy 5 business days; performance-assessed 20 (no notification/referral), 50 (referral, assessment manager), 70 (public notification, panel/SCAP); restricted 95; building consent class 1/10 20 (+10 SCAP referral); land division 60; plus 5 business days verification up front and 2 business days to issue; AND a documented clock-SUSPENSION confounder (info requests, up to 12 weeks, clock restarts) that the register does not publish per application - the latency label must declare this as a limitation, and a published late decision is still needed as the known-event fixture. Secondary label, binary: refusal = per-consent DecisionDetails DRT in {Refused, Rejected} for the planning consent; 0 = granted/approved; Withdrawn/Lapsed/Cancelled and still-Under-Assessment rows are censored, not negatives (coarse statuses are backend-enforced: Status=Refused/Granted search POSTs return no rows while Status='Decision Made' returns 260,311 + rows, negative validated by positive control, notes s6.5). Population: PDI-era applications (lodged >= 31 Jul 2020) in the statewide register; the register also carries 73,464 DEV-act-era rows (measured, incl. 36,067 decided 2010-2019 and 26,532 decided 2000-2009) which are a different, state-referred population and are EXCLUDED from the frame. Both label source fields live in a JSON child separate from every lodgement-time feature, so the label sources are excludable from what ships.

sources.name: PlanSA Development Application Register (live search application)
sources.api: No documented public API. Working channels probed 2026-11-06: (1) server-rendered HTML search form (GET after form requestSubmit; direct URL navigation with only query params does NOT trigger the search); (2) bootstrap-table AJAX rendering of results; (3) CSV export endpoint https://plan.sa.gov.au/development_application_register/assets/daregisterCSV?payload=<btoa(JSON)> where JSON = {ActionType:'csv', Config:'public_register', DataObject:'PublicRegisterCSV', Params:<serialized form fields>, SortExpression, RecordNumber} - read from the page's own bundle public-register.min.js?v=0.15.5 (554,758 bytes); a synthetic payload fetch from page context failed ('TypeError: Failed to fetch'), so construction must replicate the page's exact handler. Plain HTTP clients (curl) get HTTP 403 from the site WAF - the supported browser session is required, same posture as candidates/fenz-incident-data.
sources.access: Anonymous, no login. Register states: 'allows you to search, track, and access publicly available information about development applications lodged in South Australia'; applications lodged before 31 July 2020 may sit in legacy council registers instead. Search filters measured: Status (All/Under Assessment/Decision Made/Lapsed/Withdrawn/Cancelled), Decision authority (9 values), Council area (all SA councils), Lodged date from/to (dd/mm/yyyy), Act (DEV/PDI), Applicant, street/suburb, application number/ID, title vol/fol, Elements, sort (LodgedNew/LodgedOld/AppId), perpage 25/50/100, page.

split_strategy: Rows per window measured 2026-11-07 from the register's own search backend (TotalRecords; m/d/yyyy windows; see notes s6.5 table). PDI-era decided rows by lodgement year: 2020: 5,235; 2021: 34,482; 2022: 35,782; 2023: 31,356; 2024: 34,549; 2025: 33,280; 2026-to-date: 23,028 (sum 198,312; all-status totals 5,761/38,448/40,485/35,563/38,982/38,102/34,531; Under Assessment per year 252/1,613/2,428/2,403/2,862/3,867/11,101 - recent-year censoring is material for 2025-2026 windows). Intended windows (lodgement year, label population = decided rows): train 2020-2022 (75,499 decided rows), eval 2023-2024 (65,905), holdout 2025-2026-to-date (56,308). POSITIVES per window are NOT yet counted: refusal prevalence is unmeasured (the detail channel degraded before the sample could run, notes s6.3/s6.6) - the paced per-window detail sample is the one measurement gating the ready verdict, and the exact refusal count per window is construction's first worker step. Positives are expected to cluster by council and decision authority; clustered counts must be recorded before independence is claimed.

measurements.register_totals_2026_11_06: Read from the register's own result-count text in the supported browser session (UTC timestamps approximate, page clock 2026-11-06 03:30-04:15Z): default search 'We've found 299,858 development applications'; Status=Decision Made 260,174 (86.8% of all); Under Assessment 27,083; Lapsed 338; Withdrawn 10,538; Cancelled 1,725 (sum 299,858, consistent). Lodged 01/01/2026-06/11/2026: 17,733 (roughly 2,100/month, so a full lodgement year is on the order of 20k rows). Counts are the publisher's own displayed totals, not locally derived.
measurements.detail_schema_2026_11_06: Sample application 26037018 (192 THE PARADE NORWOOD SA 5067, lodged 5 November 2026, fetched 2026-11-06): Application summary tab shows Application ID, Lodged date, Application number ('N/A' for this one), Applicants, Assessment Pathway 'Accepted', Elements 'Internal fitout', Council area 'Norwood Payneham and St Peters', Title 'CT 5613/456 F139146 AL66', Public Notification 'Not applicable', status pill 'DECISION MADE'. Assessment tab shows per-consent decisions: 'This application requires Building Consent / Development Approval - Planning, Building' both 'Granted'. NO decision date displayed on this sample (decided within ~1 day; date-only display, so decision latency is measured to the day at best). List columns: Reference number, Applicant, Property address, Description, Lodged.
measurements.status_vocabulary_2026_11_06: Extracted from the register's own bundle public-register.min.js (PRstatusObj, verbatim descriptions): Lodged 'The application has been formally lodged by the applicant and is ready for assessment.'; Under Assessment '...awaiting decision.'; Approved 'The is approved.'; Decision Made 'Assessment of this application has completed and a decision has been made.'; Granted 'The is granted.'; Decision Under Appeal 'The decision made on the application by the relevant authority is being appealed in court, and may be upheld or overturned.'; Cancelled 'The was cancelled.'; Withdrawn 'The applicant has withdrawn this application from assessment and no decision may be made.'; Refused 'This was refused.'; Rejected 'This was rejected.'; Lapsed 'The decision made on this application has lapsed and is no longer valid.' The coarse search filter offers only Under Assessment/Decision Made/Lapsed/Withdrawn/Cancelled; Granted/Refused/Rejected/Approved/Decision Under Appeal are detail-level statuses.
measurements.access_cost_2026_11_06: plan.sa.gov.au returns 403 to plain curl (WAF) - supported browser required. In-session timings: Status-only search settles ~3-8 s; date-window searches settle 30-90 s (2026 window ~25-30 s; a 2021 window did not settle within 75 s); results render via bootstrap-table AJAX after the count text. perpage max 100 rows/page => ~3,000 pages for the full register, or windowed CSV exports via the payload endpoint (row cap unmeasured - the in-page click of 'Download .CSV of results' did not deliver a file to the browser workspace in-session; the payload recipe is recorded in sources[0].api).
measurements.au_comparator_registers_2026_11_06: data.gov.au catalogue sweep for DA/consent registers (anonymous package_search, scripts retained in probe/): City of Adelaide 'Current Development Applications' cc-by but ceased updating 2021-03-19 (dead); City of Playford per-year CSV DA register (2013 onward, cc-by, statutory Regulation 98 register - viable small fallback); ACT ACTGOV completed/active DAs via ACTmapi ArcGIS Hub (licence 'Other' - unverified); Moreton Bay QLD DAs via ArcGIS Hub (licence 'Other', weekly updates since 2016-02-01 - unverified); Victorian 'Building Permit Activity Data' per-year XLSB 2009-2026 (Building and Plumbing Commission, cc-by, >40 fields per permit, but permits issued with no decision-outcome field - carries no target). PlanSA is the only live statewide register with per-application decision statuses under a class-A licence.
measurements.nz_coverage_2026_11_06: Per this tick's regional focus: data.govt.nz catalogue is bot-walled for plain HTTP (Imperva, 'Pardon Our Interruption') but opens in the supported browser. Search 'resource consents' returned 327 datasets, dominated by regional council GIS layers (Horizons 91, Environment Canterbury 86, Otago RC 33, ...), formats HTML 319 / ArcGIS REST 282 / CSV 275, licence facets showing ~79 CC-licensed vs 9 'Other licensing'. NZ council resource-consent registers are activity permits (discharges, water takes) - a different population from first-instance development decisions, and licence verification per publisher would be required before any probe. No NZ candidate opened this tick; existing NZ candidates fenz-incident-data and nz-ea-wholesale-price-exceedance remain with their owners.
measurements.prior_art_scan_2026_11_06: Task-level prior art search (web, 2026-11-06): (1) ConfidentPlanner github.com/athuler/ConfidentPlanner - London planning approval-likelihood tool on the GLA London Planning Datahub (OGL v3), logistic regression + TF-IDF description embedding, AUC ~0.73, trained 2022-26; a tool with a trained model, NOT a published benchmark with splits/scored contract, and a different jurisdiction/decision system. (2) Lin et al. 2025, Sage J. Urban Planning 'Transforming urban planning through machine learning' - classifies Australian planning applications into development categories from description text (DeBERTa-v3 F1 0.944); text classification, not decision prediction; data available 'on reasonable request', not published ML-ready. (3) Aggregate accountability reporting only: Victoria reports '66% of all applications were processed within the statutory timeframes in 2023-24 (84 days median)'; NSW publishes council league tables of DA timeframes; RBA/Productivity-Commission 2025 housing-construction-productivity paper documents statutory-timeframe regimes per state (incl. SA) - all aggregate, none per-application, none a prediction task. Nearest family members in our own portfolio: pins-planning-appeal-outcome (GB, appeals of refused applications - different instant and population) and tc-gv-licence-application-outcome (operator licensing). No ML-ready per-application DA decision/latency benchmark with splits found anywhere; the statutory-timeframe compliance target in particular has no published predictor at all.
measurements.worked_example_2026_11_06: Dated example (all dates Australia/Adelaide, ACDT UTC+10:30; register displays dates only, so instants are day-granular): application 26037018, 192 The Parade Norwood SA 5067. Feature event window: everything up to lodgement on 05/11/2026 - description 'Commercial' (internal fitout), applicant Jones Lang LaSalle, Assessment Pathway 'Accepted', elements 'Internal fitout', council 'Norwood Payneham and St Peters'. First availability: present in the register search results when fetched 06/11/2026 ~03:55Z, i.e. within one day of lodgement (publication latency bounded at ~1 day by this one observation, not proven generally). Eligibility cutoff: lodged via the portal on/after 31/07/2020 (PDI Act); DEV-Act rows exist for some authorities. Prediction instant: lodgement, 05/11/2026 (ACDT). Target start/end: the decision event; observed status 'DECISION MADE' with 'Development Approval - Planning, Building - Granted' by fetch time 06/11/2026 ~04:15Z, so this application's decision window closed within ~1 day of lodgement (Accepted pathway; not representative of notified/assessed pathways). For a forward framing the whole target window follows the prediction instant; for this retrospective example the decision had already occurred at fetch time.
measurements.pdi_year_counts_2026_11_07: Search-backend TotalRecords per lodgement year (m/d/yyyy windows, Status filter; table in notes s6.5): decided 2020-2026 = 5,235 / 34,482 / 35,782 / 31,356 / 34,549 / 33,280 / 23,028 (sum 198,312); all-status 5,761 / 38,448 / 40,485 / 35,563 / 38,982 / 38,102 / 34,531; under assessment 252 / 1,613 / 2,428 / 2,403 / 2,862 / 3,867 / 11,101. All-time decided (status-only query): 260,311. Counts are the publisher's own backend totals read via the TotalRecords column; the response's Count field is unreliable (0 with rows present).
measurements.endpoint_layer_2026_11_07: Three machine endpoints reverse-engineered from the page's own bundle and verified (notes s6.1): CSV export (GET plan.sa.gov.au/.../daregisterCSV?payload=btoa, 7 columns, coarse status only, m/d/yyyy date parsing - dd/mm strings with day>12 return 0 bytes), search (POST cdn.plan.sa.gov.au/prs/fFGE56_reg8R, TotalRecords authoritative), per-application detail (POST same endpoint, DataObject per register code: DAP->DAPRegisterDetail, LUA/LUC->LandUseRegisterDetail, LDE->LandDivisionRegisterDetail, MD->MajorDevelopmentRegisterDetail) with 9 named children; DecisionDetails rows carry [decision type, decision, decision date]. Verified example: app 6154 'Development Approval / Granted / 30 Apr 2021' (lodged 1 Apr 2021). plan.sa.gov.au and the CDN 403 plain curl; all recipes run from browser page context.
measurements.csv_truncation_hazard_2026_11_07: MEASURED (notes s6.4): the CSV export returns a NON-DETERMINISTIC ~789,151-byte subset when a window's full result exceeds that size - dual-fetch of the identical full-year-2020 decided query gave equal byte counts (789,151) but different content (in-page hash, t1!==t2); five identical calls parsed 2,287/3,022/3,052/4,188/4,349 rows, all below the backend's 5,235. Parser determinism proven by double-parse (identical counts). Sub-~780 KB windows are complete (Sep-2020 696 rows/102 KB; Q4-2020 1,266/299 KB; half-months 2021-2026 478-1,944/72-294 KB). Construction must enumerate in month-scale windows and reconcile against TotalRecords. Descriptions contain unquoted newlines (measured examples) - quote-aware parsing plus row validation required; one 2025-09 half-month response carried 250,490 bytes with only 80 parseable rows.
measurements.detail_channel_degradation_2026_11_07: MEASURED (notes s6.3): after ~100 detail POSTs (bursts), the same query that returned full DecisionDetails for app 6154 began returning hollow children (children present, FieldValues empty), and a 30 s pause did not restore it in-session; a 16-POST foreground batch and all later reads came back hollow. Trigger undetermined (burst pacing vs backend load vs time-of-day) - unmeasured. Consequence: refusal prevalence and per-consent availability rate are UNMEASURED; extraction must pace (>= 1.5 s), validate every row, re-fetch on hollow reads, and never read an empty DecisionDetails as 'no decision'.
measurements.population_two_eras_2026_11_07: Act filter totals (search backend, 2026-11-07): DEV 73,464 + PDI 226,568 = 300,032 (= register total). Decided rows lodged 2000-2009: 26,532; lodged 2010-2019: 36,067. The register ingests the old Development Act register back to at least 2000 - a different (state-referred) population from the PDI-era all-council register; excluded from the task frame. Register-code mix from CSV samples: 2020 LUA 736/LDE 2,649/DAP 803 (whole-year fetch); DAP ~99% from 2021; LUC appears 2026. Detail DataObject must be chosen per row's register code.
measurements.status_filter_validation_2026_11_07: The coarse-status design is backend-enforced: search POSTs with Status='Decision Made' return TotalRecords 260,311 with rows, while Status in {Refused, Granted, Approved, Rejected} return no TotalRecords and no rows (same param shape, positive control working). There is no enumeration channel for refusals other than per-application detail fetches.
measurements.statutory_timeframes_2026_11_07: Pathway timeframes read 2026-11-07 from the publisher's own guidance (plan.sa.gov.au 'Stages and timeframes' + 'Guide to Development Assessment' PDI PDF, via web search snippets): planning consent deemed-to-satisfy 5 business days; performance-assessed 20 (no notification/referral) / 50 (referral, assessment manager) / 70 (public notification, panel or SCAP authority); restricted 95; building consent class 1/10 20 (+10 if SCAP referral); land division 60; all plus 5 business days verification and 2 business days to issue; performance-assessed clocks can be SUSPENDED for information requests (up to 12 weeks, clock restarts) - a per-application latency label must carry this as a declared limitation since suspensions are not published per application. Full regulation-text extraction (PDI (General) Regulations 2017) and a published-late-decision known-event fixture remain open items for construction design.
measurements.gen_star_ratings_probe_2026_11_07: GEN (federal AU, the other recorded regional next action): Star Ratings quarterly data extract series verified on gen-agedcaredata.gov.au - 15 quarterly service-level extracts May 2023 -> October 2026 (publisher: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing; 1-5 overall + 4 sub-category ratings; latest released 13 Oct 2026; site licence CC BY 4.0 was read 2026-10-31 and recorded then). The extract itself (XLSX ~2 MB on health.gov.au) could NOT be fetched from this host: health.gov.au hangs/fails for curl (two attempts, HTTP/2 stream error rc=92 then timeout) and the browser download channel does not deliver files in this environment. No candidate opened; the one-extract probe stays recorded and blocked on a working fetch channel (worker fetch or operator network).

next_action: Discovery-owned paced detail pass (one session, no worker money): re-probe the detail channel in a quiet window with >= 1.5 s spacing and a hollow-read re-fetch protocol; sample ~30 PDI-era decided applications per split window (drawn via month-scale CSV windows, m/d/yyyy, kept under ~780 KB - see notes s6.4) across DAP/LUA/LDE/LUC codes; measure (a) DecisionDetails availability rate under pacing, (b) refusal prevalence per window, (c) DD date presence. If refusals appear in all three windows: record the check-novelty verdict (ours: first-instance statewide SA per-application statutory-latency/refusal prediction at the lodgement instant with measured two-era population separation; theirs: ConfidentPlanner London tool, aggregate league tables, Lin et al. text classification) and set status ready with exact row counts + sample-measured positives, naming the full-detail-sweep extraction (~260k paced detail POSTs, CSV month-window enumeration reconciled against search TotalRecords) as construction's first worker step. If the channel stays hollow at every pacing, record the access blocker and park with the re-open condition (a paced/worker channel that returns validated consent rows). Also pending from the record: PDI statutory-timeframe known-event fixture (a published late decision), and the DEV-era rows are excluded unless separately scoped.
